cocotb_benches.dau_axi_burst_reader_tb Width-parameterized burst-reader bench: an AXI4 read-slave model serves a deterministic memory image (each 32-bit lane = its global word index) with periodic backpressure, and the collected stream must reproduce the image exactly at every DATA_WIDTH tier — the same contract at 64/128/256/512 is the precompiled-catalog guarantee. Handshake discipline: sample every valid/ready pair in the ReadOnly phase (stable pre-edge values), apply state and drive next-cycle values after the clock edge. cocotb_benches.dau_axi_random_probe_tb The random-read probe: does outstanding depth actually buy throughput? This bench does not check a data transform – it checks that the mechanism the DRAM-backed join would depend on works at all. Three claims, in the order they matter: every probe returns. A read master that loses a transaction reports a fast run and a wrong answer, so the checksum must be non-zero and the response must never be an error. the depth is really reached. peak_outstanding says how many reads were genuinely in flight. A tile that claims MAX_OUTSTANDING=16 and only ever holds one would measure the memory correctly and the design wrongly. cycles per probe FALL as depth rises. This is the whole argument: at depth 1 the rate is 1/latency, which is what dau_axi_burst_reader gets and what makes a DRAM-backed join impossible. If depth does not help here, it will not help on silicon either. The RAM model’s READ_LATENCY stands in for the DRAM round trip. The absolute numbers are the model’s, not a board’s – what transfers is the SHAPE of the curve. cocotb_benches.dau_datetime_format_tb The datetime formatter against its golden, character for character. This tile shipped without a bench, which an audit caught: its only test read constants out of the SystemVerilog and exercised the Python golden, so the HDL was never instantiated. A resource number for a module nobody ran is a number about an unverified design, and that is what this file fixes. Every case compares the 152-bit output beat against format_datetime_rows by decoding it back to a string, so a wrong character fails with the two strings side by side rather than with a hex mismatch. The dates chosen are the ones the era arithmetic gets wrong when it is written by hand: 2000 is a leap year (divisible by 400), 2100 is not (divisible by 100 but not 400), and 2024-02-29 must exist. The range ends are here because a formatter that silently truncates the year is exactly the failure DOMAIN exists to prevent. async cocotb_benches.dau_datetime_format_tb._send(dut, rows) -> None Drive rows, one handshake at a time. Sampling happens in ReadOnly and the cycle advances on RisingEdge, which is the palette’s shape. Combining send, drain and status-watch into one loop deadlocks – the sender holds input_valid while the same loop is trying to observe the output, so neither side ever fires.

async cocotb_benches.dau_datetime_format_tb._run(dut, rows, *, expect: int | None = None, ready_pattern=None) Send rows concurrently while draining. This tile declares ``success_close_out: False``, so a clean batch is contractually SILENT – there is no status beat to wait for, and a bench that waits for one hangs forever. That is not a tile defect; 23 of the 45 registered operators are silent on success, and the registry fact is the authority. So the drain ends when the expected rows have arrived, and only an ERROR produces a close-out. expect is how many rendered rows to wait for (default: all of them). ready_pattern stalls the sink, which is the backpressure case.

cocotb_benches.dau_hash_grouped_aggregation_tb._needs_slots(count: int) -> bool Skip predicate for cases whose POINT is holding several groups at once: at a table too small for them the case would test the overflow path instead, which its own case already covers. async cocotb_benches.dau_hash_grouped_aggregation_tb.hash_grouped_is_permutation_invariant(dut) The property the ordered tile cannot have: the answer does not depend on arrival order.
async cocotb_benches.dau_hash_grouped_aggregation_tb.hash_grouped_colliding_keys_probe_correctly(dut) Keys congruent modulo CAPACITY share a hash slot; the linear probe must keep them distinct.

async cocotb_benches.dau_hash_grouped_aggregation_tb.hash_grouped_overflow_is_a_defined_close_out(dut) A new key with the table full invalidates the batch — never an eviction, never a silent drop, and never a partial the host could double-count against its own re-run.

async cocotb_benches.dau_hash_grouped_aggregation_tb.hash_grouped_overflow_mid_batch_drains_and_recovers(dut) Overflow NOT on the final row exercises the DISCARD path: the rest of the batch is consumed, one error close-out is raised, and the NEXT batch starts from clean state.

async cocotb_benches.dau_hash_grouped_aggregation_tb.hash_grouped_reports_group_count_and_one_close_out(dut) group_count reads the batch’s emitted groups, and exactly one close-out is raised — checked by stalling status_ready first, so a tile that dropped or repeated it would fail here.

cocotb_benches.dau_record_gearbox_tb Record gearbox: wide beats in, one WHOLE RECORD PER CYCLE out. Correctness here is nearly trivial — the gearbox is a pure reframing, so the golden is the identity on the record sequence. The property that justifies the core is the RATE, so this bench measures it: under continuous valid input and an always-ready sink it must sustain one record per cycle, which is what turns a 3-cycles-per-record front into a 1-cycle one. A version that was correct but slow would pass a values-only bench and be worthless. async cocotb_benches.dau_rolling_extremum_tb.rolling_extremum_backpressure_both_sides(dut) Backpressure must not change a value or reorder a row: the network is a pipeline, and a skid slot sits between it and the output.

async cocotb_benches.dau_rolling_extremum_tb.rolling_extremum_resets_per_symbol(dut) The segment boundary is the whole point: a new symbol must not see the previous symbol’s values, however extreme they were.

async cocotb_benches.dau_rolling_extremum_tb.rolling_extremum_all_warmup_emits_nothing_and_closes_out(dut) A stream that forwards NOTHING still closes out. Zero forwarded rows is the one outcome a downstream tile cannot tell apart from a stall, which is why this tile is silent on success only while it is forwarding.

async cocotb_benches.dau_rolling_extremum_tb.rolling_extremum_last_rides_the_final_forwarded_row(dut) The final input rows may all be warm-up. output_last still has to land on the last row actually forwarded, so the skid holds it back until the stream ends.

async cocotb_benches.dau_rolling_extremum_tb.rolling_extremum_reuses_across_batches(dut) A SECOND batch after input_last must be a fresh window. Every other test resets first, which is exactly how a tile that carries its segment state across a batch boundary passes a whole bench. Here the second batch opens with the SAME symbol the first one closed on: if the run length survived, its first rows emit during what should be warm-up.

async cocotb_benches.dau_rolling_extremum_tb.rolling_extremum_zero_row_close_out_fires_exactly_once(dut) The close-out is a pulse, not a level. The condition is derived from a latched ‘stream has ended’ bit, so without a fired-once guard it re-asserts every cycle and a consumer holding status_ready sees an unbounded run of transfers.

cocotb_benches.dau_row_predicate_filter_width_tb The row predicate filter at element types other than int32. The tile’s row is a fixed 128-bit transport unit; the field TYPE says how many fields that row carries. So int16 packs eight values per row where int32 packs four, which is the reason to support narrow types at all – more values per beat, not a smaller beat. This bench is separate from the 32-bit one on purpose. That one pins the q6/q19 field map and its directed vectors; this one is generic over the field type and proves the parameter actually works rather than merely elaborating. It compares against a golden computed here from Python ints, with sign interpretation at the field width under test – the case a zero-extending implementation gets wrong. The type is passed by SPELLING and resolved through the same dau_core.element_types the registry uses, so what the bench drives and what a composition would ask for are the same value. q16.16 is exercised alongside the integers because it is the case a width cannot express: 32 bits wide like int32 but a different type, ordered by the identical comparator (scaling by 2**-F preserves order), which is exactly the claim the tile’s fi

Draw again until there is headroom rather than weakening the constraint – the rejection is the point.

async cocotb_benches.dau_row_unpack_slots_tb.bypass_short_final_beat_is_not_torn(dut) REGRESSION. At SLOTS == 1 an input beat is half a quad row, so input_last on phase 0 really is a torn row. At SLOTS > 1 the beat holds SLOTS/2 WHOLE quad rows, and a batch with an odd number of rows ends exactly there – rejecting it as torn refuses a well-formed stream. The generalization inherited the SLOTS == 1 rule unchanged, so this passed review and simulation until an independent reader asked what phase 0 MEANS when a beat carries whole rows.

async cocotb_benches.dau_row_unpack_slots_tb.a_layout_that_could_forge_the_pad_is_rejected(dut) REGRESSION. The all-ones packed word is the ragged-tail PAD at SLOTS > 1. A field layout covering all 64 bits can PRODUCE all-ones from real data – four unsigned 16-bit fields at max – and that row would be dropped by the wide tiles. The same input unpacks normally at SLOTS == 1, so the ANSWER WOULD DEPEND ON OUT_WIDTH. Rejecting the layout makes the sentinel unreachable by construction rather than by convention. Every real packing has room: SF1 q6 is 56 bits, q1 is 41.

dau_core._lazy Import a package’s exports on first use. Every model in this stack is a ccflow model, and importing ccflow imports csp, pandas and the rest of its stack: about 0.9 s. A package whose __init__ imports its model modules therefore pays all of it just to be imported – including when hydra’s searchpath plugin imports the config package to discover what is installed, which is the slow step in composing the registry and wants none of those names. So a package declares which submodule provides each exported name and this builds the __getattr__ that imports the one submodule the name needs. The names stay importable exactly as before (from dau_core import RegisterOffset), and a type checker reads them from the TYPE_CHECKING block the package keeps beside the declaration. class dau_core.composition.ScanCompositionSpec(/, **data: Any) Bases: dau_core.models.CheckedModel One scan fanned to len(lanes) lanes with per-lane output regions and the NoC lane register block. Two fan-out shapes: the default broadcasts the scan to every lane (each lane’s optional partition filter selects its rows), or a shared partitioner (e.g. the range partitioner) routes each row to exactly one lane — lanes then carry no per-lane partition. An optional front_unpack feed transform (the row-unpack core) sits between the burst reader and the fan-out: it widens PACKED rows (half the DDR bytes) into the standard 16-byte quad rows, so the fan-out still sees the clean 32-bit key it partitions on. It coexists with either fan-out shape. An optional front_gearbox sits in the same feed position but reframes rather than widens: it turns wide beats into ONE WHOLE RECORD per cycle, so the fan-out behind it routes records instead of rows. Its bus is therefore a record size, not a row width. Create a new model by parsing and validating input data from keyword arguments. _validate_load_phase_shape() -> None The two-phase load shape (v1): a tile binding cfg_load to the reserved load_phase symbol is driven by the shell’s LOAD_PHASE register, making the composition two-phase (a LOAD job streams the tile’s build image; a PROBE job streams rows). The LOAD image must reach every load tile unmolested, so the shape is constrained: every lane’s chain[0] is the load tile (uniformly — a loadless lane would misread the image as rows), no partition filters, no shared partitioner (the broadcast delivers the image to every lane), no front unpacker (it would re-slice image words), and — for a BITMAP_64 load tile — KEY_SPACE a multiple of 128 so the KEY_SPACE/64-word image lands on the 16-byte input length grid (QUAD_ROWS images are 16-byte rows, always on the grid).

The canonical text captures the effective design: if a model default ever changes, old and new specs produce different text rather than silently sharing a cache key. The cost is that growing the spec model changes hashes (a safe cache miss); that evolution is the explicit job of SPEC_CANONICAL_VERSION.

dau_core.composition.build_id_from_spec_hash(value: str) -> int The 64-bit identity a shell advertises for a spec, from that spec’s hash: the leading 64 bits of the digest. A shell’s capability words cannot identify a design. Distinct designs routinely advertise the same lane count, operator bitmap, host-opcode bitmap and sort capacity – q19-scan and q19-packed-wide are identical across all four – so a host asking “is the device running the design I flashed” gets a yes from a board running something else. The spec hash distinguishes them by construction, and 64 bits of it fits the identity block’s BUILD_ID register pair. Truncation is safe for this use. BUILD_ID answers “is this the design I expect”, where the alternative is a handful of shells built by the same people, not an adversary searching for a collision; the full hash stays in the manifest for anything stronger. Zero is reserved: an unstamped shell reads back as zero, so the caller must treat it as “not stamped” rather than as a design identity. KNOW WHAT THIS DOES NOT IDENTIFY. The canonical form is written against the registry, so a text from an older version can name a tile this palette no longer carries, and spec_from_canonical() then raises UnknownCoreError — an error that names the registry, which is not the thing at fault. class dau_core.cores.IngestRate(/, **data: Any) Bases: dau_core.models.CheckedModel A stream core’s guaranteed sustained ingest rate: rows rows per per_cycles clock cycles, an exact rational (1 row per 2 cycles is the composed lane rate the silicon proved; the key-mask dispatcher ingests 1 per 1). This is PUBLIC INTERFACE, not a heuristic: the scheduler/pricing software rate-matches a core it cannot inspect — a user-provided custom core tied to a custom operator is opaque except for its registry declaration, so the declaration carries the rate. Declare the FLOOR a core sustains under continuous valid input, with RECORD/DRAIN EMISSION AMORTIZED over the batch: close-out records, top-k drains, and per-group records are batch-tail or per-group costs, not per-row costs, so the declaration describes the streaming regime (groups much smaller than rows, drains at close). Data-dependent worst cases — every group key distinct, adversarial key runs into one dispatcher lane — are planner-regime concerns the planner sees in the plan (group keys, sortedness), not floor violations. A core may burst faster, and a measured improvement (a retime, a wider port) lands here the same release the RTL pr

dau_core.element_types Element types: what a value IS, not how wide it is. A registry parameter that says 32 says a field is 32 bits. It does not say whether those bits are a signed integer, a Q16.16 fixed-point number or an IEEE-754 binary32 – three things a tile must treat differently and which a width cannot distinguish. This module gives the palette’s element types names (“int32”, “q16.16”, “float64”) and turns them into the single integer a SystemVerilog parameter can carry. THE ENCODING is stated in dau_core/hdl/types.svh and mirrored here, because Verilog cannot read Python and the registry cannot read a header. test_element_types.py holds the two to the same numbers. [7:0] total width in bits (1..255) [15:8] fractional bits (0 for integers and for floats) [16] 1 = IEEE-754 binary floating point [17] 1 = unsigned A PLAIN SIGNED INTEGER ENCODES AS ITS OWN WIDTH, so int32 is 32 – the number the palette already carried. Migrating a parameter from a width to a type therefore changes no synthesized bit, no measured envelope, and no staged design; only the types a width could never express encode to anything new. dau_core.exp_generator Renders the fixed-point exp tile from a declared operating point. The datapath is dau_core.fixed_point.ExpDatapath and the emitted SystemVerilog mirrors ExpDatapath.evaluate() step for step, so the cocotb bench can compare against it with zero tolerance like every other tile. The operating point – internal precision, table size, polynomial degree, whether Horner steps round – arrives as configuration, which is why this is a generator and not a checked-in file: the 256-entry table of 2**(j/256) is a function of those parameters and SystemVerilog cannot compute it. The datapath is PIPELINED, one multiply per stage, chosen after measuring what a multiply costs rather than from the estimate this docstring used to quote. Measured on the dpv1 Artix (2026-08-09, the registry’s points): 50 DSP48s at the exact point and 20 at the light one, against 740 on the part. Folding onto a shared multiplier would cut that to roughly a ninth, but at one row per nine cycles against sqrt’s and divide’s one per three – the tile would become the bottleneck of any chain it joined. dau_core.fixed_point Integer models of the fixed-point transcendental datapaths. Two layers, and the distinction is the whole accuracy contract: exp_reference() is the MATHEMATICAL answer – true exp correctly rounded to the fixed-point format. It is what “right” means. ExpDatapath is an ALGORITHM: a specific range reduction, table and polynomial at a specific internal precision. The HDL mirrors it exactly, so the cocotb benches compare against it with zero tolerance, like every other tile in the package. An operating point that deviates from the reference does so by a MEASURED amount, swept exhaustively over every representable input and recorded in the registry beside the resource envelope. Accuracy is a measured fact here, not a claim – sampling reported one configuration as flawless when an exhaustive sweep found three wrong inputs, so nothing is believed without the full sweep. See dau-docs-private/design/transcendental-tiles.md for how the operating points were chosen. class dau_core.fixed_point.LnDatapath(/, **data: Any)[source] Bases: dau_core.models.CheckedModel One operating point of the ln datapath. x is normalised to m * 2**e with m in [1, 2), so ln(x) = e*ln2 + ln(m). The mantissa’s top table_bits index two tables – ln(1 + j/N) and the reciprocal 1/(1 + j/N) – reducing the residue to |v| <= 1/N before a short Horner series for ln(1+v). The reciprocal table is what keeps the polynomial degree low without a divider: a direct series on [0,1) would need many more terms. The exponent term is EXACT integer work: e is a small signed integer and ln2 a constant, so the only approximation is the mantissa series. class dau_core.fixed_point.NormalCdfDatapath(/, **data: Any)[source] Bases: dau_core.models.CheckedModel One operating point of the normal-CDF datapath. Folds on symmetry (the CDF of -x is one minus the CDF of x), so only the positive half is approximated, then evaluates a PER-SEGMENT Taylor polynomial: the magnitude’s top table_bits select a segment and the coefficients are the CDF’s derivatives at that segment, which have closed forms in the density. Piecewise rather than one polynomial because the CDF has no useful global series. Saturation is exact rather than a clamp: beyond the domain the correctly rounded answer IS 0 or 1, so this tile is TOTAL and needs no error path – the one transcendental here that does not. dau_core.generators Cores whose HDL is RENDERED rather than checked in. Most tiles are a hand-written .sv beside their registry entry. A few cannot be: this one needs 256 entries of 2**(j/256) to 52 bits, and SystemVerilog has no way to compute a transcendental at elaboration. The constants have to come from somewhere, and the choice is between committing a generated file that silently drifts from the parameters that produced it, or rendering it from those parameters on demand. Rendering is the same shape as everything else here: the generator is a ccflow CallableModel reached through the registry, its parameters are config, and the rendered text is a typed result. A core declares one in its registry entry and dau-build renders it before synthesis; nothing imports a generator directly, so the public build package can drive a private core’s generator without importing it. The rule that makes this safe is in CoreDefinition.source_path(): a generated core REFUSES to hand out a path until it has been rendered. The alternative – rendering implicitly on first read – hides which parameters produced the file sitting on disk, and that file is what gets synthesized. Attributes RenderContext

dau_core.hero The temporal-finance hero workflow: the predeclared end-to-end pipeline composed from the dau_core.temporal goldens, plus the avoided-materialization cost model that is the paper’s core evidence: quotes ─┐ ├─> backward as-of ─> [market-feature map] ─> time bars ─> rolling moments trades ─┘ (align) (derive, fused) (bar) (roll) The argument the model makes precise: the pipeline is a cardinality funnel. The align stage emits one market row per matched trade (N_mkt); the bar stage reduces those to a handful of bars per symbol (N_bar << N_mkt); the roll stage runs over the bars. A staged execution writes each stage’s output to DDR and the next stage reads it back — so it pays to materialize the large N_mkt market intermediate the bar reduction is about to discard. A fused execution keeps every intermediate on-chip and touches DDR only for the input stream and the final rolling output. The gain is not a magic primitive: it is the avoided DMA of the intermediate the bar reduction discards. dau_core.ln_generator Renders the fixed-point ln tile from a declared operating point. The datapath is dau_core.fixed_point.LnDatapath and the emitted SystemVerilog mirrors LnDatapath.evaluate() step for step, so the cocotb bench compares against it with zero tolerance like every other tile. Generated rather than checked in for the same reason exp and the normal CDF are: the 256-entry tables of ln(1 + j/256) and 1/(1 + j/256) and the series coefficients are transcendental constants at the configured internal precision, and SystemVerilog cannot compute those at elaboration. ln adds one thing exp does not have: LEADING-ZERO NORMALISATION. x is split as m * 2**e with m in [1, 2), and ln(x) = e*ln2 + ln(m). The exponent half is EXACT integer work – a priority encode, a barrel shift and one multiply by a constant – so only the mantissa series approximates. That is why the accuracy question is confined to the polynomial: the registered point is FAITHFUL (measured 1 ULP), and the deviation is a measured fact recorded in the registry, not a tolerance in the bench. The lessons the exp tile paid for are repeated here rather than rediscovered: every product gets its own full-width wire, and e

dau_core.models Frozen models that validate at use. Every dau-core model is frozen, and construction validates it. Two things get past that. model_copy(update=...) builds a new instance without running a single validator, so a copy can carry a value construction would have refused. And a frozen model can still hold a dict, which anyone holding the model can change in place. CheckedModel closes both. Its instances re-validate whenever they are handed back to pydantic (revalidate_instances="always"), so a parent built from a copied child refuses a bad child, and check() is that re-validation on demand: a validated copy, or the error. replace() is the validated form of model_copy. A mapping field annotated ReadOnly is stored as a FrozenMapping, which compares, hashes and serializes as the dict it was built from and refuses every mutation. The ccflow result and callable models cannot change base; they take CheckedMixin and the same config entries by hand. A Mapping rather than a dict subclass: a subclass only overrides the mutating methods, and dict.__setitem__(m, k, v) reaches past any override, so the design that LOOKS safer is the one with a hole in it. Nothing here can write, there is no inherited method that can, and the mapping hashes by content so a frozen model holding one stays hashable. It reads as the dict it was built from – equality, membership, iteration order, dict(...) – and the ReadOnly annotation carries the serializer that puts a plain dict back on the wire, so the canonical composition JSON (the design-cache key) is unchanged.

dau_core.normal_cdf_generator Renders the normal-CDF tile from a declared operating point. Generated for the same reason the exp tile is: its per-segment Taylor coefficients are transcendental constants at the configured internal precision, and SystemVerilog cannot compute them at elaboration. The emitted SystemVerilog mirrors dau_core.fixed_point.NormalCdfDatapath.evaluate() step for step, so the cocotb bench compares against it with zero tolerance like every other tile. That model is correctly rounded over EVERY representable input, so for this tile the algorithm and the mathematics coincide. Pipelined one multiply per stage, which is what the exp measurements forced: a DSP48’s clock-to-out is ~3.5 ns, so a carry chain sitting between two of them overruns 8 ns. A fixed-point root is an integer root in disguise. With x = X * 2**-f, the result sqrt(x) * 2**f is sqrt(X * 2**f) — so the answer is isqrt(X << f), floor-truncated like every other fixed-point result in this package (the multiply-shift convention). This is worth stating because the obvious implementation is a polynomial approximation, which would need an error bound and would still be wrong in the last place. There is no approximation here and no tolerance in the bench: the tile either matches this or it is broken. Raises on a negative input; the tile reports DOMAIN for the same case.

Raises outside the representable range; the tile reports DOMAIN for the same case rather than emitting a truncated year.

dau_core.operators.fixed_point_divide(numerator: int, denominator: int, *, fractional_bits: int = DIVIDE_FRACTIONAL_BITS) -> int[source] Quotient of two Q``(32-f)``.``f`` fixed-point values, EXACTLY. With a = A * 2**-f and b = B * 2**-f, the result (a/b) * 2**f is (A << f) / B — an integer division, so there is nothing to approximate and the bench compares with no tolerance. FLOOR, not truncation toward zero. That is the convention the rest of the package already uses: MULSHR divides by a power of two with an arithmetic shift, which floors, and -7 >> 1 is -4. Python’s // floors too, so this is simply that operator. A tile that truncated toward zero would disagree with the existing map ALU on every negative operand. Raises on a zero divisor, and on a quotient that does not fit int32; the tile reports DOMAIN and RANGE for those cases.

class dau_core.operators.FieldSumAggregate[source] The one record the field-sum aggregation tile emits per batch: exact INT64 sums of the mask-selected fields (ascending field order) plus the row count. classmethod from_record_words(words: collections.abc.Sequence[int], *, field_mask: int) -> FieldSumAggregate[source] The inverse of record_words(): read one lane’s emitted record back into the aggregate it describes. A host reading results off a device has the same record and the same mask, so the decode is not a second statement of the format but this one run backwards – which is why it lives here rather than in whichever host layer happens to read the bytes. Every caller that hand-rolled the unpack got to choose its own word order and its own sign convention; this cannot. words is one unsigned 64-bit word per mask-selected field in ascending field order, then the count. Sums are two’s complement and come back signed; the count does not.

classmethod combine(records: collections.abc.Sequence[FieldSumAggregate]) -> FieldSumAggregate[source] The record one lane would have emitted over the union of the rows several lanes each saw a DISJOINT share of: sums add, counts add. This is the partition algebra of the tile – what makes a key-mask dispatcher’s replicas, or a complete pair-key partition group, answer as one lane – and it holds only under a partition. Folding two lanes that each saw every row counts every row twice, which is a fact about who fed the lanes and not about this fold; the caller that knows the fan-out decides what is combined.

class dau_core.operators.MembershipBuildSet(/, **data: Any)[source] Bases: dau_core.models.CheckedModel The membership memory: a direct-mapped EXACT bitmap over the configured dictionary-id key space [0, key_space). Key k is a member iff 0 <= k < key_space and bit k is set. Addressing decision (and its exactness). The IN-list / semi-join key column is dictionary-encoded host-side (dau-polars) into dense ids [0, N), and key_space is that dictionary’s cardinality rounded up to a multiple of 64. Because every id maps to exactly one bit, membership is EXACT — no false positives AND no false negatives — over the id space. A full 2**32 bitmap would be 512 MB, impossible; the bounded dictionary space is the natural fit and keeps the whole memory BRAM-resident. A probe key outside [0, key_space) is definitionally a non-member: the build set only ever holds in-range dictionary ids, so an out-of-range probe key (signed int32, so negatives and ids >= key_space included) cannot be in it. This is the honest, verifiable v0; MembershipKind.BLOOM is the future inexact alternative for unbounded key spaces (host-verified false positives). The bitmap loads as key_space // 64 little-endian 64-bit imag

A scan split into overlapped batches is one dedup, and summing per-batch counts would count a key once per batch it appears in — so the accumulation runs until the host asks for a fresh one (cfg_clear on the batch that starts it), and the final batch’s count is the answer. Feed a result’s seen back in to model the next batch of the same accumulation; pass nothing to model one that cleared first.

The membership filter’s bitmap is STATIC: loaded in a build phase, then probed read-only. This one is written as it is probed — if the row key’s bit is clear, set it and count the row; otherwise the key has been seen and the row changes nothing. That single difference (insert on probe) is what a distinct needs and what a static bitmap cannot do, and it is why the tile pays a read-modify-write per row where the filter pays a read. Sized by CARDINALITY, not by row count: the bitmap holds one bit per distinct key, so the memory is set by how many distinct keys exist, not by how many rows carry them. dau_core.operators.keyed_asof_join_rows(records: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int, int, int, int]], *, tolerance: int | None = None) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int, int, int]][source] Golden semantics for the generic keyed backward as-of join tile: one host-merged, (key, time)-sorted stream of BUILD and PROBE records (build-before-probe at equal key/time). Each record is (rec_type, key, time, a, b) — rec_type bit0: 0 = build, 1 = probe; a/b are two opaque INT32 payload fields. Because the stream is key-grouped, exactly one build is live at a time: a build updates the held (time, a, b) for its key (reset on key change), and a probe attaches the most recent build with build_time <= probe_time (within tolerance on the time axis, None = unbounded), emitting the joined row (key, time, probe_a, probe_b, build_a, build_b). A probe with no live build (or one older than tolerance) drops — the tile emits matched joins only. Workload-agnostic: the temporal-finance backward as-of (quote = build {bid, ask}, trade = probe {price, size}) is exactly this join, and dau_core.temporal.asof_backward() on sorted inputs agrees with it.

Order is preserved. Every build and probe key must lie in [0, key_space) — an out-of-range key is ERR_RANGE on the tile and raises here. All fields are INT32 (two’s-complement wraparound). dau_core.operators.gearbox_records(words: collections.abc.Iterable[int], *, record_words: int, record_count: int) -> list[tuple[int, ...]][source] Golden semantics for the record gearbox: a pure REFRAMING. The input is a flat stream of 64-bit words carrying record_count back-to-back records of record_words words each, delivered in beats that need not divide the record size — so records straddle beat boundaries and the tail beat may be padded. The output is the record sequence, unchanged: no field is inspected, reordered or dropped, so the golden is the identity and the interesting property is the RATE (one whole record per cycle) rather than the values. Words beyond record_count * record_words are beat padding and are ignored; too few words is a framing error the hardware reports as ERR_STREAM.

dau_core.operators.mask_dispatch_records(records: collections.abc.Iterable[collections.abc.Sequence[int]], *, num_partitions: int, mode: DispatchMode = DispatchMode.MASK) -> list[list[tuple[int, ...]]][source] Golden semantics for the key-mask dispatcher over N-WORD records. The quad-row form (mask_dispatch_rows()) routes two 64-bit words keyed on the first word’s low half. A fused chain whose head reads wider records — the as-of join’s three-word {tag/key, time, payload} — routes those records WHOLE on the same key, so a per-symbol workflow can be replicated across lanes without reshaping the stream. Each record is a sequence of 64-bit words; the routing key is word0 & 0xFFFFFFFF read as a signed 32-bit value, exactly the hardware bit-select. Order is preserved within each partition.

dau_core.operators.mask_dispatch_rows(rows: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int, int, int]], *, num_partitions: int, mode: DispatchMode = DispatchMode.MASK) -> list[list[tuple[int, int, int, int]]][source] Golden semantics for the key-mask dispatcher: route each (key, value, aux0, aux1) row to partition key & (num_partitions - 1) (num_partitions a power of two; the signed 32-bit key’s low bits — two’s complement, so negative keys mask exactly like the hardware bit-select), order preserved within each partition. The pair-key partition (key & mask == lane) moved from N per-lane filters into one shared router. Returns one ordered list per partition. DispatchMode.EXACT_BRANCH selects the exact-branch-id mode (q19’s disjunct branches): partition key - 1 for keys in [1, num_partitions], every other key dropped at the router (branch 0 — and any negative key, whose unsigned 32-bit image exceeds any partition count — costs zero lane cycles). It needs no power-of-two. DispatchMode.HASH multiplies the key by DISPATCH_HASH_MULTIPLIER and takes the TOP log2(N) bits of the low-32-bit product. MASK reads the key’s LOW bits, so it spreads keys evenly only when those bits already vary — diction

dau_core.operators.stride_distribute_rows(rows: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int, int, int]], *, rows_per_beat: int, num_partitions: int) -> tuple[list[tuple[int, int, int, int]], ...][source] Route packed rows by static slot position and per-slot round robin. Row i occupies slot i % rows_per_beat. Each slot owns one contiguous group of num_partitions / rows_per_beat lanes and advances only its own round-robin counter. This is correct for keyed aggregation even though a key may reach several lanes: the host merges per-lane partials by key, the same partial-group contract used by q1’s two-pass aggregation.

dau_core.operators.pack_splitters(values: collections.abc.Sequence[int]) -> str[source] Pack range-partitioner splitter constants into the cfg_splitters SV bus literal {32'h..., ...}. cfg_splitters is a flat bus carrying splitter i at [i*32 +: 32]; SV concatenation packs MSB-first, so the highest-index splitter is emitted first (reversed). The partitioner compares keys and splitters as signed 32-bit values (range_partition_bar_rows); values that would wrap under the & 0xFFFF_FFFF pack are rejected.

class dau_core.operators.TopKErrorCode[source] Bases: enum.IntEnum Status codes for the streaming top-k heap tile. Initialize self. See help(type(self)) for accurate signature.

dau_core.operators.streaming_top_k(rows: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int, int, int]], *, k: int) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int]][source] Golden semantics for the streaming top-k heap tile: in one pass keep the k rows with the largest signed-32-bit sort key (field 0), breaking ties by arrival order (earlier rows win), and emit them sorted by sort key DESCENDING (ties arrival ascending) — the ORDER BY <key> DESC LIMIT k shape (q3/q10, TSBS group-by-order-by-limit). Bounded state: the tile holds at most k rows in a size-k min-heap whose root — the eviction target — is the entry with the smallest key and, among equal-key entries, the LATEST arrival (the heap orders on (key, -arrival), not key alone). An arriving row replaces the root only when its key is STRICTLY greater, so at the k-th-largest key the earliest arrivals are retained — matched by the (-key, arrival) sort below. This root tie-order is part of the tile contract: a key-only min-heap could evict an earlier tied row and diverge from this golden. k is bounded to [1, TOP_K_MAX]; the tile reports BAD_K outside that range.

dau_core.operators.time_bucket_key_rows(rows: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int, int, int, int]], *, bucket_shift: int, bucket_bits: int) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int]][source] Golden semantics for the generic time-bucket key tile: rewrite each row’s partition key into a composite (partition, time-bucket) group key so a downstream key-grouped aggregator produces fixed-width time-windowed groups per partition. Window = 2**bucket_shift; key = (partition[:PART_BITS] << bucket_bits) | (time >> bucket_shift)[:bucket_bits] with PART_BITS = 32 - bucket_bits. Input rows are (partition, payload_hi, time, payload2, payload3); output the aggregator’s quad rows (key, payload_hi, payload2, payload3). Workload-agnostic — any time-windowed aggregation composes it before the generic aggregator.

dau_core.operators.gather_records(words: list[int], *, in_words: int, out_words: int, selectors: tuple[int, ...]) -> list[int][source] Gather 32-bit halves from fixed-width records into new records. Each packed selector uses bits [5:0] for source-word index, bit 6 for source half (0 low, 1 high), and bits [11:7] for a logical right shift; bits [31:12] are reserved and must be zero. Selectors are ordered by output half: low half, then high half, for each output word. Shifts always zero-fill, including when the selected half has its sign bit set.

dau_core.operators.grouped_field_aggregate_rows(rows: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int, int, int]]) -> list[GroupedFieldAggregate][source] Golden semantics for the generic multi-field grouped aggregator (ordered close-out): consecutive rows with equal keys form a group; each of the three data fields (v0, v1, v2) gets its first/last/min/max/sum in one pass, plus the row count. A reappearing key opens a NEW group (partials merged host-side, the partial-group contract) — workload-agnostic; OHLCV bars are a selection over it (see bars_from_field_aggregate()).

dau_core.operators.bars_from_field_aggregate(groups: collections.abc.Iterable[GroupedFieldAggregate]) -> list[BarAggregate][source] OHLCV bars as a field/stat SELECTION over the generic multi-field aggregate: price = field 0 (open/close/low/high = first/last/min/max), shares = sum of field 1, frac = sum of field 2. The finance column assignment lives here, not in the aggregator.

dau_core.operators.bar_aggregate_rows(rows: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int, int, int]]) -> list[BarAggregate][source] Golden semantics for the fused bar-aggregation tile (ordered close-out): consecutive rows with equal keys form a bar; volume is shares * SCALE + frac recombined on the host.

A key that reappears later opens a NEW group — partials are merged by the host, never the tile.

dau_core.operators.keyed_state_scan(rows: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int]], *, op: KeyedStateOp, capacity: int, initial: int = 0) -> tuple[list[tuple[int, int]], KeyedStateErrorCode][source] Golden semantics for the keyed state tile: a per-key accumulator updated once per row, emitting the POST-UPDATE state for every row. This is the primitive the stateful family is built on. Unlike every tile that precedes it, the output for a row depends on rows that came before it with the SAME key — a loop-carried dependency per key, which is exactly the shape a SIMD CPU cannot vectorize and a spatial datapath can hold on-chip. rows are (key, value) pairs in arrival order. Each row reads its key’s current state, applies op, writes it back, and emits (key, new_state). A key seen for the first time starts from initial, so the first row of a key emits op(initial, value) — NOT value, unless op is SET. That distinction is the whole reason initial is explicit rather than implied. Emitting post-update state, not pre-update, is a deliberate contract. Post-update is what a running aggregate means, it is what the hardware can produce without an extra pipeline stage holding the old value, and it

dau_core.operators.scratchpad_scan(rows: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int, int]], *, granted_words: int) -> tuple[list[tuple[int, int]], ScratchpadErrorCode][source] Golden semantics for the scratchpad tile: the deliberately trivial consumer of the OWNED storage class (STORAGE_AND_NOC.md). A private word-addressed arena; each row is (write_enable, addr, value) and emits (addr, post_op_value) — a write emits what it wrote, a read emits what is stored, an unwritten word reads 0 (BRAM init). The contract under test is the GRANT, not the arithmetic: an address at or past granted_words is STORAGE_OVERFLOW — a defined close-out that preserves already-emitted rows, exactly the shape a grow-request replaces when the allocator hardens. Addresses and values are int32 wires (wrapped); a negative address is never inside any grant.

dau_core.operators.sessionize_scan(rows: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int]], *, gap: int, capacity: int) -> tuple[list[tuple[int, int, int, int]], SessionErrorCode][source] Golden semantics for the session-gap tile: the Nexmark-Q11 shape over bounded keyed state (STORAGE_AND_NOC.md). Rows are (key, time) in arrival order; a session is a maximal per-key run of rows with no inter-row gap exceeding gap. Each closed session emits (key, start_time, end_time, row_count). Sessions close two ways. A row whose time exceeds its key’s last time by more than gap closes the old session (emitted immediately, in arrival order) and opens a new one. Batch end closes everything still open, emitted sorted by signed key — a deterministic order no implementation detail (hash placement, slot index) can leak into. Scope is PROCESSING-order sessionization: times must be non-decreasing across the batch (the generator’s contract), and a violation is TIME_ORDER — refused, never silently reordered. Event time, watermarks and late arrivals are deliberately absent here. capacity bounds DISTINCT KEYS per batch, exactly like keyed state: a gap-close immediately reopens, so it never frees a slot mid-batch.

dau_core.operators.hash_grouped_field_sum_rows(rows: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int, int, int]], *, field_mask: int, capacity: int) -> tuple[list[HashGroupedAggregate], HashGroupedErrorCode][source] Golden semantics for the HASH-mode grouped field-sum aggregation tile: one INT64 accumulator set per DISTINCT key in a bounded on-chip table, drained key-ascending at close-out. The difference from grouped_field_sum_rows() is the whole point of the tile: the ordered tile groups CONSECUTIVE equal keys, so a key that reappears after another key opens a second partial group the host must merge, and the staged table must be pre-sorted on the group key. This tile holds a per-key accumulator, so input order does not matter and a key may reappear anywhere in the batch — one record per distinct key, always. That removes the sorted_by_key staging precondition from every grouped scan. Two contracts are deliberate and must be honoured bit-for-bit by the HDL: Emission is key-ASCENDING (signed). A hash table has no intrinsic order, so leaking the probe/slot order into the record stream would make the result depend on the hash function — an implementation detail no golden could pin and no ho

dau_core.operators.merge_hash_grouped(partials: collections.abc.Iterable[collections.abc.Iterable[HashGroupedAggregate]]) -> list[HashGroupedAggregate][source] Merge per-batch hash-grouped partials into one key-ascending result — the host half of the overflow contract. Splitting a batch (by key range, or simply into smaller batches) and merging the partials is EXACT: INT64 sums and row counts are additive per key, and no other state crosses a batch boundary. This is what makes GROUP_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED a recoverable condition rather than a failed query, and the property merge(split(rows)) == one_shot(rows) is the test that keeps it honest. Every partial must carry the same field_mask; mixing masks is a caller error, not a merge case.

dau_core.records Byte layouts of the rows and records the grouped and bar tiles exchange with the host. A layout is a tuple of (field, kind) pairs in wire order, little-endian, with kind a numpy-style code (i4, u4, i8, u8). The tiles’ registry entries declare the same records in 64-bit words (record_words and output_record_words), and the suite checks the two agree, so a tile that changes its record width fails there rather than on the host. Field names follow the goldens’ result types (GroupAggregate, BarAggregate); pad fields hold no data and keep the wider fields on their natural alignment. class dau_core.registers.HandleTableControlFlag[source] Bases: enum.IntFlag The WRITE bits of HandleTableRegisterOffset.CONTROL: which of the staged entry’s two commits the write performs. Both are one-cycle pulses, so they always read back zero – CONTROL reads report the resolution state instead. Here rather than in the host, for the same reason the offsets are: a bit position a programmer carries in their head is how a free ends up installing. A host stages one commit or the other; the table resolves the collision in free’s favour, which is a safety net, not a sequence. Initialize self. See help(type(self)) for accurate signature.

They sit at the top of the code space, below the shell’s own 0xFE length-gate fault, because that space is the shell’s: a tile’s error codes are small and per-core (dau_core.operators), and a fault that refuses the job outright is not one of them. Composition IS the registry: the definitions live in dau-core’s hydra config tree (dau-core/cores.yaml) composed into the ccflow ModelRegistry at /dau-core/<core-name>, and there is no Python-literal core list anywhere. These accessors are thin views for in-process consumers – tests, shell walking, source staging. They are deliberately NOT part of the tile authoring surface. A third party declaring a tile needs the models in dau_core.cores; it must never need this module, which knows only about the tiles dau-core itself ships. Keeping the two apart is what lets the surface be reachable by an author who does not have this repository – see tests/test_public_tile_surface.py, which enforces the direction. Composition IS the registry — there is no Python-literal core list; these accessors are thin read-through views for in-process consumers (tests, dau shell walking). A /dau-core subregistry a consumer already composed (possibly with overrides) is the source of truth and is never reloaded or overwritten here; the packaged defaults load only when it is absent. dau_core.temporal Golden models for the temporal-finance hero workflow. The fused workflow this file is the CPU reference for: quotes ─┐ ├─> backward as-of ─> midpoint/spread/sign ─┐ trades ─┘ ├─> time/vol/$ bars └─> rolling features Everything here operates on the encoded integer domain the hardware sees — symbol ids are int32 dictionary codes, timestamps are int64, prices/sizes are int64 fixed-point (the host quantizes at a chosen scale before staging, exactly as dau_polars.ohlcv does with its micro-unit SCALE). The models are therefore scale-agnostic integer arithmetic: a caller that quantizes price and size at scales Sp and Ss gets dollar volume in Sp*Ss units and must express dollar-bar thresholds in the same units. Division is deferred (Q100 discipline): bars and rolling windows emit exact integer accumulators (sum / sum-of-squares / count) and the host divides once, so every value on the wire is exact. State is bounded and per-symbol: the as-of tile holds one current quote per symbol partition; a bar tile holds one open bar; a rolling tile holds one window. The pre-sort precondition (both streams ordered by (symbol_id, time)) is the same one the sorted-scan tiles already req

class dau_core.temporal.RollingMoment[source] The exact integer accumulators of one full rolling window — mean and variance divide once on the host (moment_mean(), moment_var()).

dau_core.temporal.rolling_moments(values: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int]], *, window: int) -> list[RollingMoment | None][source] Per-symbol rolling (count, sum, sum_of_squares) over the last window values — the deferred-division form of rolling mean/variance. REFUSES a window whose sum of squares leaves a signed 64-bit accumulator. That is the tile’s arithmetic precondition, and it binds inside the int32 domain: (2**31-1)**2 is already 2**61, so a full-range int32 column overflows sum_sq from window 3. The tile cannot check it — it sees one row at a time and has no bound to compare against — and it wraps silently into a wrong variance rather than erroring. Python integers do not wrap, so a golden that computed the exact value would DISAGREE with the hardware over exactly the inputs the contract excludes, and the bench comparing the two would be the only thing that ever noticed. Raising instead keeps the reference and the datapath from ever quietly parting company: inside the precondition they are equal, and outside it neither claims an answer. The proof properly lives further upstream — dau-polars refuses to route a rolling scan whose value column declares no magnitude_bi
dau_core.temporal.moment_mean(moment: RollingMoment) -> float[source] Mean from a rolling moment.

dau_core.temporal.moment_var(moment: RollingMoment, *, ddof: int = 1) -> float[source] Variance from a rolling moment (ddof=1 sample variance, matching polars.rolling_var). Raises on an under-determined window. The numerator count*sum_sq - sum*sum is formed in exact integers before the single float divide — dividing sum*sum first (float) would cancel the variance away at fixed-point magnitudes (e.g. three consecutive values near 1e9).

dau_core.temporal.moment_std(moment: RollingMoment, *, ddof: int = 1) -> float[source] Sample standard deviation from a rolling moment. The root of moment_var(), and deliberately defined in terms of it rather than independently: polars’ rolling_std is the root of its rolling_var, so any other formulation would disagree with the reference in the last place for no benefit. On device this is where the divide and sqrt tiles land – variance divides before it roots – which is why the numerator stays exact integers right up to the single divide.

dau_core.temporal.ewma(values: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int]], *, alpha: float) -> list[float][source] Per-symbol exponentially weighted moving average, non-adjusted recursion (e[0] = x[0]; e[i] = alpha*x[i] + (1-alpha)*e[i-1]) — matches pl.col(x).ewm_mean(alpha=alpha, adjust=False).over("symbol"). Float: the reference real-valued semantics the fixed-point tile approximates under its declared error budget.

dau_core.temporal.deltas(values: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[int | None][source] Per-symbol first difference (value[i] - value[i-1]; None for the first row of each symbol) — matches pl.col(x).diff().over("symbol").

dau_core.temporal.generate_market_stream(*, seed: int, num_symbols: int = 4, quotes_per_symbol: int = 24, trades_per_symbol: int = 40, price_scale: int = 1000000) -> MarketStream[source] Generate a deterministic quote/trade fixture: per symbol, a random-walk two-sided quote (micro-dollar prices) and interleaved trades in integer share sizes priced near the prevailing midpoint — so dollar_volume accumulators stay comfortably in int64. Same seed ⇒ byte-identical output (replay determinism). Uses only the stdlib random — zero-dependency, like the rest of dau-core. exhaustive_sweep Exhaustive accuracy sweeps for the fixed-point transcendental datapaths. A bound is only ever what was actually swept. This arc has four recorded cases of a sample declaring a datapath flawless that the full domain disproved – Q48/degree-5 exp, the 256-segment CDF, ln at 60,000 samples, and ln again at 663,000 – so a registered accuracy fact comes from here, not from a stratified sample. THE COST IS THE REFERENCE, NOT THE DATAPATH. ln_reference and its siblings compute in 80 decimal digits so that half-way cases double cannot decide are decided correctly. Calling that for every input puts a full 2**31 sweep in the tens of core-hours (an estimate from the per-input cost when this was written, not a timed run). Deciding in double and re-deciding only the inputs that sit too close to a rounding boundary brings it down to minutes on a workstation, because only a few thousand inputs are close. Both answers are identical; only one is affordable enough to run on every candidate operating point. This module was written after the slow estimate had sent a candidate light point to the back of the queue as a multi-session task. It is committed so the capability is not rediscov

test_benches_can_fail Prove the benches can fail. A bench that always passes and a bench that checks nothing are indistinguishable from a green suite, and this project has now shipped several of the second kind: a scan bench that raised before comparing and so never compared, a verilator install that could not build any timing bench, and a device check whose field was read from a snapshot that never populated it. Every one of those was found by hand or by an adversarial reviewer. None was found by the suite, because a suite only reports what a test asserts, and none of them asserted that the check ran. The check here is mutation. Take a tile whose bench passes, change its SystemVerilog so it computes the wrong answer, and require the bench to FAIL. Together with the existing pass-on-clean-source tests that is a two-sided proof: the bench distinguishes a correct implementation from an incorrect one, which is the only property that makes a green bench mean anything. Mutations are chosen to be semantic and small — an off-by-one in a count, an inverted comparison — so a bench that survives one is not merely insensitive to a wholesale rewrite. They are applied to a COPY; the registry’s

test_composition.test_a_sized_tile_prices_at_its_size_not_its_default() -> None A parameter that changes the hardware has to change the price. This assertion used to be the OPPOSITE – that a 6M-key membership filter priced identically to a default 4096-key one – and it was true only because the tile carried a scalar envelope that answered every KEY_SPACE with the same numbers. The membership filter is a BITMAP, so its BRAM cost IS the key space: 1 BRAM36 at 4096, 192 at 6,000,000, which is 57% of the Artix’s 335 budgeted blocks. Every composition using the silicon-proven configuration was priced at 1/192 of the BRAM it actually places.

test_composition.test_spec_hash_pinned_fixture() -> None The design-cache key must be stable across releases: ANY change to the canonical form — field ordering, a new or changed spec field or default, hash construction — fails HERE, loudly, and must bump SPEC_CANONICAL_VERSION deliberately (defaults are included precisely so a changed default changes the key instead of colliding).
test_composition.test_spec_from_canonical_revalidates() -> None A tampered canonical form fails registry validation, never builds.

test_composition.test_canonical_version_reads_the_prefix_a_recorded_hash_carries() -> None The prefix is what a reader has instead of the palette that wrote the text beside it, so it has to be readable without one.

test_composition.test_a_text_recorded_under_an_older_palette_is_refused_by_version_not_by_parse() -> None The defect this boundary closes, in one place. A build manifest written before the width-named tiles were renamed records a canonical text naming them. Reading it against today’s registry raises UnknownCoreError — an error about a missing tile, from a design that is built, flashed and answering. The version prefix beside the text is the fact that says the text predates this palette, and it says so without a parse.

test_composition.test_handle_table_capacity_is_design_identity_and_inert_at_zero() -> None A handle table is HARDWARE — a table of flops and a resolve stage in front of the reader — so a design that carries one must not share a cache key with one that does not, and eight slots is not sixteen. Zero is the no-table default: a spec that never mentions it keeps the shape it has today and round-trips unchanged.

test_composition.test_wide_data_width_composition_rules() -> None The canonical spec mirrors the walker’s width rules: a wide feed needs a dispatcher (broadcast is 64-bit only), wide packed reads are a typed follow-up, and the tier set is closed.

test_composition.test_throughput_reproduces_the_measured_rate_ladder() The rate model recomputes silicon: 64-bit two-beat = 1/2 row/cycle (~99 ms q6), the 512-bit dispatch feed = 1 (the serializer, 60.3 ms measured 2026-07-30), and MORE LANES DO NOT HELP past the dispatcher’s declared ingest — the motivation for the wide-sum lane / distributor.

test_composition.test_the_wide_lane_shape_composes_and_rate_matches() The wide lane: one lane of wide-row-stream stages consuming reader beats directly — SLOTS rows per cycle, no partitioner. The q6 shape at 512 rates 4 rows/cycle (the parallel-row target).

test_composition.test_the_fused_chain_shape_is_declared_not_inferred() -> None A terminal-shaped tile mid-lane (the temporal hero’s as-of join and grouped aggregator) composes only when the spec DECLARES the fused chain: the refusal still catches an aggregator dropped into a chain by accident, while the declaration says the caller accepts that mid-stage close-outs are drained and only their errors reach the lane status.

test_composition.test_selectivity_reconciles_the_model_with_q6_silicon() -> None The rate benches measured the q6 map stage at one row per SEVEN cycles standalone, which made the no-selectivity model predict 1/7 for q6 — 3.4x below the 0.483 rows/cycle silicon actually ran. Both numbers are right: two predicates upstream pass ~2% of rows, so the map never binds the feed. Charging each stage against the rows that reach it restores agreement, and the worst case stays the default because selectivity is data-dependent.

test_composition._record_dispatcher(record_words: int = 3) -> dau_core.composition.TileSpec The dispatcher as it sits BEHIND a gearbox: its bus is one whole record wide, so it takes RECORD_INPUT rather than a row framing.

test_composition.test_front_gearbox_reaches_core_names_and_resources() -> None The gearbox must appear in core_names: that tuple is what stages the HDL a build compiles, so a gearbox missing from it is instantiated by the generated top and never handed to the toolchain — the design black-boxes at synthesis.

test_composition.test_a_geared_design_does_not_share_a_hash_with_an_ungeared_one() -> None The spec hash keys the design cache. If the gearbox were invisible to the canonical form, a cached ungeared bitstream would be handed back for a geared design and silently run the wrong front.

test_composition.test_the_gearbox_is_charged_as_the_front_delivery_it_is() -> None A GUARANTEED floor has to charge the stage that produces the rows. The gearbox was validated by five walkers and priced by none: absent from this function, a geared composition took the quad-row delivery of data_width/128 – 24-byte records charged as 16-byte ones – and the gearbox’s own one-record-per-cycle ceiling was never applied at all. At data_width=512 that reports 4 rows/cycle for a front that sustains 1.

test_composition.test_a_wider_record_lowers_the_geared_delivery() -> None The record size is the DIVISOR of the reader’s supply, so it has to move the answer – a delivery term that ignores it is the shape that charged 24-byte records at the 16-byte quad-row rate.

test_composition.test_a_gearbox_record_mismatch_is_detected() -> None stream_shape_mismatches exists to find exactly this, and the front stage it never looked at was the gearbox: a 3-word gearbox feeding a 4-word dispatcher validated clean and the detector returned ().

test_composition.test_a_stream_job_composition_declares_its_own_infrastructure() -> None A stream job stages one tile chain through its job core instead of reading bursts and fanning out. Until it could be declared, its cores reached the build as a hand-copied list — so nothing checked that the list still matched what the top instantiates.

test_composition.test_a_stream_job_composition_refuses_scan_shaped_fields() -> None The stream job has no fan-out and no burst feed, so accepting a partitioner or a front stage would let a spec describe hardware the shell cannot build.

test_composition.test_the_scan_shell_still_requires_a_lane_counter() -> None The count_port waiver is the STREAM job’s, not a general relaxation: the scan shell’s record writer sizes its write-out from that port.

test_composition.test_addr_width_is_32_or_64_only() -> None A job master of some intermediate width is not hardware anyone builds, and permitting it would mean carrying padding logic through every register slice for a shape with nothing behind it: the AXI-Lite read path zero-extends cleanly at exactly 32 and 64 and needs an explicit pad at anything else.

test_composition.test_a_packed_front_can_feed_a_wide_lane() -> None The packed feed and the wide lane compose. Each is silicon-proven alone and they were mutually exclusive: the wide lane read whole quad rows straight from the reader, so it burned 16 bytes of DDR per row, and the next SLOTS doubling would have demanded 19.2 GB/s from a 12.8 GB/s DDR3. Packed, the same lane demands 9.6. Two widths are in play and they are NOT the same number. data_width is the READ width – SLOTS packed 64-bit rows per beat – while the lane downstream of the unpacker sees SLOTS whole 128-bit quad rows. Note the consequence: an unpacked SLOTS=8 lane would need data_width=1024, which is not a legal tier, so packing is what puts eight slots in reach at all.

test_composition.test_a_packed_wide_feed_rates_at_the_unpacker_not_at_one_row() -> None The packed feed’s ceiling is the READER’s packed-row supply, which is data_width/64, not a flat one row per cycle. The flat cap read the packed path as “one 8-byte row per 64-bit beat”, true only while data_width was 64. A packed WIDE feed hands the unpacker data_width/64 packed rows per beat, and capping at 1 under-reported the silicon-measured eight-slot lane by 8x – the design would have been priced as no faster than the build it replaced.

test_composition.test_shell_infrastructure_is_selected_by_role_not_by_name() -> None Composition IS the registry: the shell cores a composition places are the ones declaring each infrastructure role, exactly one per role, and composition.py names none of them. The order the scan roles are placed in is pinned because core_names feeds the canonical hash.

test_cores.committed_hdl(hdl_dir: pathlib.Path) -> set[str] | None The HDL git CARRIES under hdl_dir, as paths relative to it, or None when there is no repository to ask. Committedness is a git fact, and only git can answer it. A directory listing cannot: the suite renders every generated core into the render root on each run (conftest._render_generated_cores), so a rendered file being PRESENT there is the normal state and says nothing about whether someone checked it in. Absent a repository – an installed distribution – nothing is committed and there is nothing to check.

test_cores.test_every_hdl_file_belongs_to_exactly_one_core() -> None Checked-in HDL and registry entries match exactly, in both directions. A GENERATED core is excluded because it has no checked-in file by definition – and asserted to have none, which is the same guard from the other side: a generated core with a file beside the entry means someone committed rendered output, and whichever of the two is stale will be the one that gets synthesized. The reach is the whole package, not one directory listing. Listing hdl/ alone left the render root – a SUBDIRECTORY of it – outside this guard entirely, and three rendered tiles sat committed there until a rename made their filenames disagree with their contents. So the walk descends, and the committed set comes from git: a rendered file being present in the render root is the normal working state (the suite renders there on every run), and what distinguishes that from the mistake is whether it was checked in.

test_cores.test_every_selectable_operator_declares_its_ingest_rate() -> None Ingest rate is core PUBLIC INTERFACE (the scheduler rate-matches opaque cores from the registry declaration alone): every stream operator declares it. The floor is the composed 1-row/2-cycle lane rate; only silicon-proven faster cores declare 1/1.

test_cores.test_every_selectable_operator_declares_its_contract_kind() -> None A new core declares its stream contract in the registry — contract tests select validators from this tag, never from test-local exemption sets.

test_cores.test_synthesizable_cores_carry_measured_envelopes() -> None Recorded operator/stream-infra envelopes are measured OOC values. EMPTY as of 2026-08-16: the stride distributor was the last operator carrying no envelope at all, and no design containing it could be priced. Asserted exactly, so a tile shipped without a measurement fails here rather than surfacing as an unpriceable design later.

test_cores.test_the_width_named_tiles_are_exactly_the_declared_ones() -> None The naming rule is that a width is a parameter, not an identity; this pins how much of the palette still contradicts it. Scoped to own_cores() for the same reason every exact-set guard here is: an installed third-party tile with a width in its name is that vendor’s business, not drift in our palette.

test_cores.test_the_canonical_palette_is_exactly_the_registered_names() -> None THE GUARD a rename has to pass. A name that leaves this set takes every recorded canonical spec that spells it with it. Scoped to own_cores() like every exact set here: a vendor’s installed tile is not in our canonical alphabet’s history and cannot depart from it. There are exactly two honest ways past a DEPARTURE failure: Keep the name. A rename that buys nothing is not worth an identity boundary. Bump SPEC_CANONICAL_VERSION and CANONICAL_PALETTE_VERSION in the same change, so every text recorded under the old palette is refused by version instead of read against a registry that cannot resolve it. Designs already on silicon do not re-enter the design cache across that boundary – their hash is stamped in a bitstream and the manifest recording it must not be rewritten – so they are rebuilt once, deliberately, rather than mis-recognized forever.

test_cores.test_the_canonical_palette_is_pinned_to_the_canonical_form_it_spells() -> None The other direction of the same coupling: a canonical-form bump that leaves this set alone has not said which palette the new version reads, and the departure message above would then name the wrong version.

test_cores._measured(**overrides) A core carrying one measurement point, built here rather than read from the registry: which cores are migrated is a migration detail, and a test of the lookup should not move when that changes.

test_cores.test_an_unclocked_measurement_answers_for_any_clock_and_records_no_timing() -> None A combinational core (identity-registers is one: a parameter ROM with no clock) has no timing to meet, so its point carries no timing status and prices a build at every clock.

test_cores.test_every_registered_core_with_resources_carries_measurement_points() -> None There is one shape for a resource record. A scalar count with no part, clock or parameters cannot say which board it was measured on and no longer parses.

test_cores.test_normalize_follows_the_same_rule_as_violation() -> None A type spelling is only for a parameter declared element_type; a plain parameter takes an int and refuses a string the way violation() does.

test_cores.test_registry_is_hydra_composition_not_a_python_literal() -> None Composition IS the registry: cores load from dau-core’s hydra config tree into the ccflow ModelRegistry at /dau-core/<name>. A parallel Python-literal core list is the anti-pattern this guards against.

test_cores.test_accessors_defer_to_a_composed_registry() -> None The composed registry is the source of truth: accessors read through to /dau-core (no snapshot cache), so a consumer’s hydra overrides are visible and never clobbered by a default reload.

test_cores.test_silent_on_success_operator_set_is_pinned() -> None The status contract’s two classes are registry truth: silent-on-success cores (chain-stage/partition legal) versus per-batch success close-out cores (terminal-tile legal). Changing a core’s class changes lane status semantics — confirm intent here.

test_cores.test_dispatcher_rate_still_needs_record_aware_modeling() -> None The dispatcher’s framing-shaped rate describes a 2-word record. Its 64-bit front ingests one WORD per cycle, so an N-word record costs N cycles, while a wide framing delivers a whole record per beat-slot — two rules the current rate shapes cannot express together. Record shape is now declared for detection, but this pins the remaining rate-model gap so RECORD_WORDS != 2 is not silently treated as resolved.
test_cores.test_an_element_type_parameter_accepts_a_width_or_a_spelling() -> None The two forms are the same declaration where they overlap, and the spelling reaches types a width never could.

test_cores.test_an_element_type_parameter_bounds_the_width_not_the_encoding() -> None A registry bound mirrors an RTL guard about BITS. q16.16 encodes as 4128 and is a 32-bit type; bounding the encoding would reject it for being a large number, which is a statement about nothing.

test_cores.test_an_element_type_spelling_is_refused_where_no_type_is_declared() -> None A size parameter takes a size. Silently reading “int32” as 32 on a capacity is the misreading the whole mechanism exists to prevent.

test_cores.test_a_measurement_coordinate_may_name_the_type_it_was_measured_at() -> None The same point, written either way, is one point – so migrating a registry entry to spellings cannot orphan an envelope that was measured before types existed.

test_cores.test_a_core_resolves_hdl_from_the_package_that_declares_it(tmp_path, monkeypatch) -> None A tile contributed by another distribution finds its own HDL. The registry is a hydra search path, so any package joining it through the hydra.lernaplugins entry point can contribute cores. Their HDL used to be resolved under dau_core.hdl regardless, so a third-party tile could be registered from anywhere but had to vendor its Verilog into this package. source_package is the seam.

test_cores.test_a_well_formed_vendor_tile_does_not_trip_our_palette_guards(monkeypatch) -> None Installing a third-party tile must not fail THIS suite. Four guards here assert an exact set over the whole registry – the HDL directory listing, the descriptor-tagged operators, the envelope-free tiles, and the scalar-envelope holdouts. Each is a statement about dau-core’s own palette, and each read loaded_cores(), so a vendor tile registered through the entry point showed up as drift in all four. A contributor’s first experience of the platform was our test suite failing on their correct tile. The line drawn is between those four and the universal-property guards (every operator has a golden, a contract kind, record words, a measured envelope). Those are contract requirements a well-formed tile satisfies, so they stay registry-wide on purpose – which is why the tile below is built well-formed rather than minimal. It is the exact-set guards that fail even a perfect vendor tile, and only those are scoped.

test_datetime_format The datetime formatter’s golden, and the constants the tile divides by. The tile has no divider: every division in it is a multiply-shift by a compile-time constant, and a multiply-shift identity is only valid over a bounded input range. Those bounds are the whole correctness argument for the arithmetic, and they live in the HDL as bare magic numbers – so this reads them back out of the .sv and proves each one against real floor division at BOTH ENDS of every quotient block, which is where such an identity fails first. A constant edited in the HDL without its range being re-derived fails here rather than in a rendered date. test_generated_cores Generated cores go through the same seams as checked-in ones. A tile whose HDL is rendered is the first thing in this registry that has no file beside its entry. That is a place where a parallel mechanism could easily grow – a build-layer side channel that renders somewhere the registry cannot see. test_hdl_elaboration.test_this_gate_actually_ran() -> None A required check that can silently carry no signal is worse than a non-required one. Every other test in this file skips on which("verilator") is None, so a tool install that quietly failed leaves the gate green having elaborated nothing. That is not hypothetical: the bench job once spent 60 minutes wedged installing verilator, was cancelled without reaching a single bench, and reported nothing about the diff while appearing to run. DAU_REQUIRE_VERILATOR turns that skip into a failure. Note what this test does NOT skip on: verilator itself. A guard that steps aside for the same reason as its subject guards nothing, so where the tier is required this runs unconditionally and fails. It lives here rather than in the workflow so the assertion travels with the tests it guards.

test_measured_from_matches_the_hdl A recorded envelope must say which RTL produced it, and still match it. Resource numbers are not self-checking. They are transcribed from a synthesis run into the registry by hand, and once written nothing in the tree can tell whether the RTL beneath them has moved since: the drift detector that would notice (synthesize_cores.parse_reports’ registered_matches) only runs when somebody runs Vivado. Two separate stale-envelope findings – row-unpack understated by ~1000 LUT at three of its coordinates, wide-field-sum-aggregation by up to 106 LUT and 141 FF at three more – trace to ONE commit with one shape: it re-measured the coordinates it ADDED and not the ones it CHANGED. Both were found by accident, months later, while attributing something else. measured_from closes that. It stamps the recorded numbers with a digest of the HDL closure they describe (CoreDefinition.hdl_closure_digest() – the tile’s own source, the packages it imports, the headers it includes), and this module recomputes it. An edit to any of those files fails HERE, naming the tile, in the fast job, seconds after the edit – which is the property that matters: the check fires on exa

test_measured_from_matches_the_hdl.test_every_stamped_envelope_matches_its_hdl_closure() -> None THE GUARD. A stamped tile’s HDL must still digest to what its numbers were recorded against. Failing here does NOT mean the numbers are wrong – it means nobody has said whether they are. There are exactly two honest ways out and neither is editing the digest to match: Re-measure the tile’s recorded coordinates through dau-build task=tasks/build/synthesize-cores and record what comes back, stamp included. Show the edit is netlist-neutral – one control coordinate reporting envelope_drift=none against the pre-change tree – and re-stamp with that evidence in the pull request.

test_measured_from_matches_the_hdl.test_the_unstamped_envelopes_are_exactly_the_declared_ones() -> None Both directions, for the reason every exact set in this suite is: a stale name means a tile got stamped and nobody tightened the guard, and an unlisted name means a measurement shipped with no record of what it measured.

test_measured_from_matches_the_hdl.test_every_core_has_a_computable_hdl_closure() -> None A closure that cannot be resolved is a defect whether or not the tile is stamped yet – otherwise a missing header or an unregistered dependency stays invisible until the day somebody first tries to stamp that tile.

Too permissive and it misses the edit that matters: a package edit must reach every tile that imports it. Too strict and every unrelated edit re-measures the world: a header a tile does not include must not reach it.

Its constants live in the generator and in the registry entry’s generator config; move either and the digest must move.

test_output_beat_declarations A tile’s declared record shape must be able to hold the beat its RTL emits. datetime-format declared output_record_words: 1 – 64 bits – while its output_data port is 152 bits wide. Its description said so in prose, in capitals, for the tile’s whole life. Prose is not what the composition layer reads: check_record_width_compatibility compares the declared word counts, and it is detection-only, so a 152-bit beat wired into a one-word consumer would have dropped 11 of the 19 characters with nothing raised. The guard is deliberately narrow. output_record_words counts words in a logical RECORD, not bits in a beat, and 35 of the 36 literal-width tiles declare MORE words than one beat holds – rolling-moments declares 3 on a 64-bit port and streams them as three consecutive beats. That is the convention and it is fine. The only thing that is never fine is a record declared too small to hold a single beat of itself, which is unsatisfiable under any beat count. Parameterized widths (OUT_WIDTH-1, SLOTS*128-1) are skipped: their width is not known until elaboration, so there is nothing to compare here. test_parameter_bounds_match_the_hdl A parameter bound stated twice is a bound that can disagree with itself. The registry declares what a tile’s parameters may be; the tile’s own elaboration guard declares the same thing in SystemVerilog, because Verilog cannot read the registry. Both are necessary. Nothing made them agree, so the registry could offer a K the tile refuses to elaborate, or – worse – accept one the tile elaborates into something unmeasured. The tiles state their bounds in a small set of conventional forms, which is what makes this checkable. A form this cannot parse is listed explicitly rather than skipped silently: an unparsed guard is an unchecked guard, and a holdout list that nobody can see is how the last audit went stale.
